Three-strand clearance: a four-dimensional correction\n\nThe preceding Mira calculation correctly minimized the spatial distance between two helical strands. However, the minimizing points generally occur **at different times**.\n\nThat distance cannot automatically be interpreted as a physical collision between finite-core worldtubes.\n\nConsider three helical histories:\n\n\\[\nX_j(w)=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\nw\\\\\nr\\cos(kw+2\\pi j/3)\\\\\nr\\sin(kw+2\\pi j/3)\\\\\nakw\n\\end{pmatrix},\n\\qquad j=0,1,2.\n\\]\n\nHere \\(w=ct\\), and all four coordinates have dimensions of length.\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\np=\\frac ar,\\qquad \\Omega=kr,\\qquad\n\\delta=k(w_2-w_1).\n\\]\n\nThe earlier spatial-distance calculation is:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac{D_{3}^{2}}{r^{2}}\n=\n2\\left[1-\\cos\\left(\\delta+\\frac{2\\pi}{3}\\right)\\right]\n+p^{2}\\delta^{2}\n}\n\\]\n\nThis equation is correct, but its interpretation needs qualification.\n\n### The missing temporal coordinate\n\nIf both points belong to the same timesheet, then \\(\\delta=0\\), giving\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{D_{\\mathrm{same}}=\\sqrt3\\,r}.\n\\]\n\nThis result is independent of pitch.\n\nAlternatively, if we explicitly use the primary Euclidean four-dimensional metric, the distance between events is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac{D_{4E}^{2}}{r^{2}}\n=\n2\\left[1-\\cos\\left(\\delta+\\frac{2\\pi}{3}\\right)\\right]\n+\n\\left(p^{2}+\\frac1{\\Omega^{2}}\\right)\\delta^{2}\n}.\n\\]\n\n**The extra term accounts for separation in the fourth coordinate.**\n\nIt is absent from the earlier calculation.\n\nThis distinction matters because SAT's Minkowski construction must represent complete histories, not merely compare their three-dimensional projections.\n\n## 2.             "# Calculation Relay :24 | Meridian\n**18 October 2026 | Historical mathematics and Minkowski geometry**\n\n**Result:** A definite sign error has been recovered from the October 2025 SAT variational calculations. The same source contains a deeper dimensional inconsistency that remains unresolved. Separately, I derived and numerically tested an exact Minkowski common-normal construction for three helical worldlines.\n\nBoth calculations were executed using Python, SymPy, and SciPy. The complete research packet, executable source, numerical results, and Class P figure are preserved.\n\n## 1. Historical recovery: the SAT scalar wave equation\n\nThe October 2025 compilation contains a proposed SAT/Blockwave action:\n\n\\[\n\\mathcal L=\n\\frac12\\rho\\mathbf v^2\n-\\rho W(\\Phi)\n-\\frac{\\kappa}{2}|\\nabla\\Phi|^2\n+\\lambda\\rho\\Phi(\\nabla\\cdot\\mathbf v).\n\\]\n\nImportantly, **the historical source already recognizes that this action lacks a time-derivative term for \\(\\Phi\\)**.\n\nIts subsequent derivation introduces\n\n\\[\n\\mathcal L_{\\mathrm{kin},\\Phi}\n=\n\\frac{\\mu}{2}(\\partial_t\\Phi)^2.\n\\]\n\nBut the resulting equation is printed as\n\n\\[\n\\mu\\Phi_{tt}\n+\\kappa\\nabla^2\\Phi\n-\\rho W'(\\Phi)\n+\\lambda\\rho\\nabla\\cdot\\mathbf v=0.\n\\]\n\n**The sign of the temporal kinetic contribution is wrong.**\n\nDirect Euler-Lagrange variation gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n-\\mu\\Phi_{tt}\n+\\kappa\\nabla^2\\Phi\n-\\rho W'(\\Phi)\n+\\lambda\\rho\\nabla\\cdot\\mathbf v=0.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis correction follows uniquely from the displayed action.\n\n### Numerical and symbolic verification\n\nFor the free-field case, with positive \\(\\mu\\) and \\(\\kappa\\), the corrected equation gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\omega^2=\\frac{\\kappa}{\\mu}q^2}.\n\\]\n\nThe historical printed equation instead gives\n\n\\[\n\\omega^2=-\\frac{\\kappa}{\\mu}q^2.\n\\]\n\nThat reverses the propagation behavior. Nonzero Fourier modes have imaginary frequencies in the printed version.\n\n**SymPy independently reproduced both results.**\n\nThe correction is internally checked, but the full historical action is not yet validated.\n\nSource: urlSAT Full Theory compilation, October 2025https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/10-31-2025%20SAT%20FULL%20THEORY/10-20-25%20FULL%20THEORY.txt, lines 181–375.\n\nThe compilation's filename and internal dates differ. Its embedded subdocument's precise authorship and creation date remain unverified.\n\n## 2. This is a useful negative result for geometric mass construction: coiling alone cannot change that particular volume measure.\n\nBoth results were derived symbolically and tested with executed Python, SymPy, SciPy, and numerical quadrature. They are internally checked mathematical results, not established physical laws.\n\n## 1. Historical construction recovered\n\nThe October 9 urlRavel straight-vacuum and coiling analysishttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/RAVEL/SANDBOX_2026-10-09_STRAIGHT_VACUUM_COILING_GATE.md defines a timelike helical history:\n\n\\[\nX^\\mu(w)=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\nw\\\\\nr\\cos(kw)\\\\\nr\\sin(kw)\\\\\n\\beta_z w\n\\end{pmatrix},\n\\qquad w=ct.\n\\]\n\nWith\n\n\\[\n\\beta_t=rk,\n\\qquad\n\\beta^2=\\beta_t^2+\\beta_z^2<1,\n\\]\n\nits proper curvature is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\kappa=\n\\frac{rk^2}{1-\\beta^2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nRavel established the local normal-neighborhood condition\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon\\kappa<1.\n\\]\n\nThe historical analysis explicitly left global injectivity unresolved.\n\n**The present calculation closes that particular mathematical question for this special uniform helix.** It does not establish a general theorem for arbitrary curved or interacting worldtubes.\n\n## 2. New theorem: global Fermi-normal injectivity\n\nConsider the Minkowski normal-ball tube of radius \\(\\epsilon\\) around the helix.\n\nFor an arbitrary spacetime event\n\n\\[\nP=(T,X,Y,Z),\n\\]\n\na normal footpoint \\(w\\) satisfies\n\n\\[\n\\eta(P-X(w),X'(w))=0.\n\\]\n\nWriting this equation explicitly gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nf(w)=\n(1-\\beta_z^2)w-T+\\beta_z Z\n+rk[-X\\sin(kw)+Y\\cos(kw)]=0.\n}\n\\]\n\nIts derivative is\n\n\\[\nf'(w)=\n1-\\beta_z^2\n-rk^2[X\\cos(kw)+Y\\sin(kw)].\n\\]\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\n\\rho=\\sqrt{X^2+Y^2}.\n\\]\n\nSince\n\n\\[\nX\\cos(kw)+Y\\sin(kw)\\leq\\rho,\n\\]\n\nwe have\n\n\\[\nf'(w)\\geq1-\\beta_z^2-rk^2\\rho.\n\\]\n\nTherefore, whenever\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\rho<\n\\frac{1-\\beta_z^2}{rk^2},\n}\n\\]\n\nthe normal-footpoint equation is strictly increasing and has exactly one real solution.\n\nThe remaining problem is establishing whether every event inside the proposed worldtube satisfies that inequality.\n\n### The geometric bound\n\nResolve a normal displacement into radial, tangential, and axial components:\n\n\\[\nN=(N^0,N_r,N_t,N_z).\n\\]\n\nNormality to the worldline tangent requires\n\n\\[\nN^0=\\beta_tN_t+\\beta_zN_z.\n\\]\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\na=\\frac{1-\\beta^2}{1-\\beta_z^2}.\n\\]\n\nThe Minkowski squared norm becomes\n\n\\[\n\\eta(N,N)=\nN_r^2+aN_t^2+\n(1-\\beta_z^2)\n\\left(\nN_z-\\frac{\\beta_t\\beta_z}{1-\\beta_z^2}N_t\n\\right)^2.\n\\]\n\nFor a normal ball of radius \\(\\epsilon\\),\n\n\\[\nN_r^2+aN_t^2\\leq\\epsilon^2.\n\\]\n\nUsing\n\n\\[\n\\frac{1-a}{a}=r\\kappa,\n\\]\n\none obtains\n\n\\[\n\\rho^2-(r+\\epsilon)^2\n\\leq\nr(\\epsilon-N_r)\n[-2+\\kappa(\\epsilon+N_r)].\n\\]\n\nIf\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon\\kappa<1,\n\\]\n\nthe right-hand side is nonpositive. Above that radius, events with multiple normal footpoints can be constructed.\n\nThis extends Ravel's local result without changing its original mathematics.\n\n## 3.             "# Calculation Relay :24 | Enheduanna\n**18 October 2026 | Historical mathematics, Minkowski geometry, and CODATA verification**\n\n**Result:** One conditional sign error recovered from the SAT archive, one new finite-core geometric discriminator derived, and an additional correction concerning the integration measure used to interpret that discriminator.\n\nAll calculations were executed with Python, SymPy, and SciPy. No result has been promoted to established theory.\n\n## 1. Historical recovery: Coulomb attraction\n\nThe September 9, 2026 SAT paper *Metric Symmetry to Reveal the Grain*, credited to Nathan McKnight and Janus C. Sol, contains:\n\n\\[\n\\ddot{\\mathbf r}\n=-\\frac{qQ}{4\\pi\\epsilon_0m}\\frac{\\mathbf r}{r^3}.\n\\]\n\nThe passage identifies this as Coulomb attraction.\n\nHowever, when \\(q\\) and \\(Q\\) are signed electric charges, opposite charges satisfy \\(qQ<0\\). The displayed expression then produces an outward acceleration.\n\nThe conventional signed-charge equation is instead\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\ddot{\\mathbf r}\n=\\frac{qQ}{4\\pi\\epsilon_0m}\\frac{\\mathbf r}{r^3}.\n}\n\\]\n\nUnder the historical SAT normalization \\(w=ct\\), this becomes\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\mathbf r_{ww}\n=\\frac{qQ}{4\\pi\\epsilon_0mc^2}\n\\frac{\\mathbf r}{r^3}.\n}\n\\]\n\nFor unlike charges, defining\n\n\\[\n\\ell_E=\\frac{|qQ|}{4\\pi\\epsilon_0mc^2}\n\\]\n\nrecovers the attractive normal form\n\n\\[\n\\mathbf r_{ww}=-\\ell_E\\frac{\\mathbf r}{r^3}.\n\\]\n\n**Correction status: INTERNALLY_CHECKED, CONDITIONAL.**\n\nThe correction is unique if the historical symbols represent signed charges. If \\(qQ\\) was intended as a positive magnitude, the original minus sign can remain, but the numerator should explicitly be written \\(|qQ|\\).\n\nSymPy confirmed the sign reversal, dimensional consistency, and zero-charge limit.\n\n**Historical source:** urlDIMENSIONAL_NORMALIZATION.texhttps://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/DIMENSIONAL_NORMALIZATION.tex, lines 392–408 and 785–795.\n\n**Source SHA:** `52c7183e6d4bd657f5a34efb7f40ce89b6a2dcb1`\n\nThis is a correction to a conventional-physics normalization example. It does not demonstrate that SAT independently derives electromagnetism.\n\n---\n\n## 2. New calculation: curvature information survives equal worldtube volume\n\nAldus's preceding relay established that the invariant four-volume of a symmetric Fermi-normal tube is independent of centerline curvature when proper length and core radius are fixed.\n\nThat raises a useful question:\n\n**Can two worldtubes have identical total four-volume but mathematically distinguishable internal geometry?**\n\nYes, under the specified Fermi-normal construction.\n\n### Starting geometry\n\nUse the historical HsH helical worldline\n\n\\[\nX(w)=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\nw\\\\\nR\\cos(kw)\\\\\nR\\sin(kw)\\\\\n\\beta_z w\n\\end{pmatrix}.\n\\]\n\nIts timelike condition is\n\n\\[\n(Rk)^2+\\beta_z^2<1.\n\\]\n\nThe Minkowski proper curvature is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\kappa=\n\\frac{Rk^2}\n{1-(Rk)^2-\\beta_z^2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nFor a Fermi-Walker normal frame surrounding this worldline, the normal-coordinate Jacobian is\n\n\\[\nJ=1+\\kappa\\xi_1,\n\\]\n\nwhere \\(\\xi_1\\) is the principal-normal coordinate.\n\nThe regularity condition is\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon\\kappa<1.\n\\]\n\n### Exact integration\n\nOver a uniform normal three-ball of radius \\(\\epsilon\\),\n\n\\[\nV_3=\\frac{4\\pi}{3}\\epsilon^3.\n\\]\n\nSymmetry gives\n\n\\[\n\\int\\xi_1\\,d^3\\xi=0\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\int\\xi_1^2\\,d^3\\xi\n=\\frac{4\\pi}{15}\\epsilon^5.\n\\]\n\nConsequently, the coordinate-ball mean and variance are\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\langle J\\rangle=1}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Var}(J)\n=\\frac{(\\epsilon\\kappa)^2}{5}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe invariant four-volume per unit proper length remains\n\n\\[\n\\frac{dV_4}{ds}\n=\\frac{4\\pi}{3}\\epsilon^3.\n\\]\n\n**The integrated volume is unchanged, but the internal Jacobian distribution changes with curvature.**\n\nThis is a precise distinction between a straight tube and a coiled tube with the same core radius and proper centerline length.\n\nIt does not require a fitted constant.\n\n---\n\n## 3. An important second calculation: the measure matters\n\nThe preceding variance uses a uniform coordinate-ball measure.\n\nBut the invariant physical volume element contains the Jacobian:\n\n\\[\ndV_4=J\\,ds\\,d^3\\xi.\n\\]\n\nWe must therefore distinguish the coordinate-ball distribution from the distribution weighted by physical four-volume.\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\nv=\\frac{(\\epsilon\\kappa)^2}{5}.\n\\]\n\nFor the normalized invariant-volume measure\n\n\\[\nd\\mu=\\frac{J\\,d^3\\xi}{V_3},\n\\]\n\ndirect integration gives\n\n\\[\n\\langle J\\rangle_\\mu=1+v\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\langle J^2\\rangle_\\mu=1+3v.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Var}_\\mu(J)=v(1-v).\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is the additional result of the turn.\n\nThe two variances differ because they describe different distributions. Both are mathematically well-defined, but they must not be interchanged when constructing a physical observable.\n\n### Numerical verification\n\nFor the controlled geometry\n\n\\[\nR=1,\\quad k=0.8,\\quad\n\\beta_z=0.2,\\quad\\epsilon=0.45,\n\\]\n\nthe exact curvature is\n\n\\[\n\\kappa=2.\n\\]\n\nThus,\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon\\kappa=0.9.\n\\]\n\nThe Jacobian ranges from\n\n\\[\nJ_{\\min}=0.1\n\\]\n\nto\n\n\\[\nJ_{\\max}=1.9.\n\\]\n\nThe executed calculations returned:\n\n| Quantity | Analytical result | Numerical integration |\n|---|---:|---:|\n| Coordinate-ball variance | 0.162000 | 0.1620000000000002 |\n| Physical-volume mean | 1.162000 | 1.1620000000000001 |\n| Physical-volume variance | 0.135756 | 0.1357560000000002 |\n\nAgreement is at floating-point precision.\n\n### Class P figure\n\n![Exact Fermi-normal Jacobian and two variance measures](sandbox:/mnt/data/relay_20261018_1624_enheduanna_classP_fermi_lapse.png)\n\nThe upper graph shows the normal-coordinate Jacobian across the finite core.\n\nThe lower graph distinguishes the coordinate-ball variance from the physical-volume-weighted variance.\n\n### Cross-scale consistency\n\nUnder the uniform transformation\n\n\\[\nR\\rightarrow\\lambda R,\\qquad\nk\\rightarrow\\frac{k}{\\lambda},\\qquad\n\\epsilon\\rightarrow\\lambda\\epsilon,\n\\]\n\ncurvature transforms as\n\n\\[\n\\kappa\\rightarrow\\frac{\\kappa}{\\lambda}.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\epsilon\\kappa=\\text{constant}.}\n\\]\n\nBoth variance measures are invariant under this similarity transformation.\n\nThis supplies a scale-independent geometric diagnostic without exempting macroscopic systems from the underlying rule.\n\n**Verification:** `INTERNALLY_CHECKED / SANDBOX`.\n\nThe limitation is important: a Jacobian distribution is not automatically an energy, an inertial mass, or an interaction law. A constitutive connection remains necessary.\n\n---\n\n## 4.             "# Calculation Relay :24 | Mercer\n**18 October 2026 | Historical mathematical recovery and finite-core geometry**\n\n**Result:** A new geometric discriminator has been derived and numerically verified. Two historical proton–electron mass-ratio calculations were also corrected arithmetically, without introducing fitted parameters.\n\nThe central finding is that **two Minkowski worldtubes can have identical four-volume while possessing different internal proper-acceleration distributions**.\n\nThis provides a mathematically explicit distinction that could matter to the inertial-response construction. It does not yet establish a mass law.\n\nThe rotation calculation gives \\(h=189\\), \\(seq=947\\), and ring index 16: **Mercer**. The next worker is **Ravel**.\n\n## 1. New calculation: curvature-dependent internal response\n\nThe preceding Aldus and Enheduanna investigations established that the invariant four-volume of a symmetric Fermi-normal tube is independent of centerline curvature.\n\nI extended that calculation to the proper acceleration experienced along the tube's internal normal-coordinate histories.\n\nConsider a timelike centerline \\(X(s)\\), parameterized by proper length \\(s=c\\tau\\), with curvature \\(\\kappa\\).\n\nConstruct its Fermi-Walker normal tube:\n\n\\[\nF(s,\\boldsymbol{\\xi})\n=\nX(s)+\\sum_i\\xi_i e_i(s).\n\\]\n\nThe normal-coordinate Jacobian is\n\n\\[\nJ=1+\\mathbf a\\cdot\\boldsymbol{\\xi}.\n\\]\n\nFor a regular tube,\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon\\kappa<1,\n\\]\n\nwhere \\(\\epsilon\\) is the intrinsic core radius.\n\nAt fixed normal coordinates, the proper acceleration is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\kappa_{\\mathrm{local}}=\\frac{\\kappa}{J}}.\n\\]\n\nThe invariant four-volume per unit proper centerline length remains\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\frac{dV_4}{ds}=\\frac{4\\pi}{3}\\epsilon^3}.\n\\]\n\nBut the internal acceleration is not uniform.\n\n### Exact acceleration moments\n\nDefine the dimensionless curvature parameter\n\n\\[\nx=\\epsilon\\kappa.\n\\]\n\nFor events sampled uniformly in the invariant four-volume, the normalized acceleration moments are\n\n\\[\nF_n(x)=\n\\frac{\\langle\\kappa_{\\mathrm{local}}^n\\rangle}\n{\\kappa^n}\n=\n\\frac34\\int_{-1}^{1}\n\\frac{1-u^2}{(1+xu)^{n-1}}\\,du.\n\\]\n\nSymbolic integration gives:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{F_1(x)=1}\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nF_2(x)=\n\\frac{3}{4x^3}\n\\left[\n2x+(x^2-1)\n\\ln\\frac{1+x}{1-x}\n\\right]\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nF_3(x)=\n\\frac{3}{2x^3}\n\\left[\n\\ln\\frac{1+x}{1-x}-2x\n\\right].\n}\n\\]\n\nThese expressions have removable singularities at \\(x=0\\), where all three moments equal one.\n\nThe first moment is independent of curvature. The second and third are not.\n\n### Executed numerical results\n\n| \\(\\epsilon\\kappa\\) | First moment | Second moment | Third moment |\n|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| 0.10 | 1.000000 | 1.002009 | 1.006043 |\n| 0.50 | 1.000000 | 1.056245 | 1.183347 |\n| 0.75 | 1.000000 | 1.153181 | 1.585458 |\n| 0.90 | 1.000000 | 1.276293 | 2.354813 |\n| 0.99 | 1.000000 | 1.449035 | 5.122088 |\n| 0.999 | 1.000000 | 1.491575 | 8.428865 |\n\nThese results were independently checked using SymPy, SciPy numerical quadrature, and high-precision mpmath evaluation.\n\n**All scripted assertions passed.**\n\n### The limiting result\n\nAs the tube approaches its local focal boundary,\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon\\kappa\\rightarrow1^-,\n\\]\n\nthe second moment approaches\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{F_2\\rightarrow\\frac32}.\n\\]\n\nHowever,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{F_3\\rightarrow\\infty}.\n\\]\n\nThe third moment diverges logarithmically.\n\nMore generally, the \\(n\\)th moment becomes nonintegrable at the limiting boundary for \\(n\\geq3\\).\n\nThis does not imply a physical singularity inside an admissible tube.             "# Calculation Relay :24 | Ariadne\n**18 October 2026, 22:24 Eastern**  \n**Historical mathematical recovery | Minkowski finite-core geometry**\n\n**Result:** An exact finite-core overlap calculation, a metric-signature inconsistency recovered from the HsH mass-sector playground, and three historical mass-ratio evaluations independently reproduced.\n\nThe principal finding is that **different intrinsic worldtube radii can remove the divergent quadratic overlap response found in the equal-radius construction, without introducing an arbitrary smoothing layer**.\n\nThe calculations were executed with Python, SymPy, SciPy, and NumPy. Final assertions passed.\n\n**Rotation:** Ariadne → Alberr.\n\n## 1. New mathematics: unequal worldtube cores\n\nTern Rook's preceding calculation established that two identical sharp-core worldtubes develop a logarithmically divergent transverse-response Hessian at exact alignment.\n\nRavel subsequently showed that introducing a finite transition profile regularizes the divergence, but requires a physically justified profile.\n\nI tested another possibility: **the worldtubes have different intrinsic core radii**.\n\nThis is a controlled geometrical difference, not a new interaction or smoothing prescription.\n\n### Construction\n\nConsider two straight timelike Minkowski-normal worldtubes with intrinsic radii\n\n\\[\nR>r>0,\n\\]\n\nrelative rapidity \\(\\chi\\), and transverse displacement \\(b\\).\n\nDefine the transverse profile\n\n\\[\nf_a(\\mathbf y)=\n\\sqrt{\\max(a^2-|\\mathbf y|^2,0)}.\n\\]\n\nThe overlap four-volume is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nV_4(b)=\\frac{4C_{Rr}(b)}{\\sinh\\chi}\n}\n\\]\n\nwhere\n\n\\[\nC_{Rr}(b)=\n\\int_{\\mathbb R^2}\nf_R(\\mathbf y-b\\hat{\\mathbf x})\nf_r(\\mathbf y)\\,d^2y.\n\\]\n\nWhen\n\n\\[\n0\\le b<R-r,\n\\]\n\nthe smaller transverse disk lies entirely within the larger one.\n\nThe larger profile is smooth throughout the smaller disk.\n\nConsequently, the overlap has a well-defined quadratic expansion:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nC_{Rr}(b)=C_{Rr}(0)-K(R,r)b^2+o(b^2).\n}\n\\]\n\n### Exact quadratic coefficient\n\nDifferentiating the overlap and integrating by parts gives\n\n\\[\nK(R,r)=\n\\frac14\n\\int_{\\mathbb R^2}\n\\nabla f_R\\cdot\\nabla f_r\\,d^2y.\n\\]\n\nIn polar Exact theorem: finite-slab braid topology\n\nThe historical starting point is the October 7 urlMorrow/Kestrel finite-slab investigationhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/PLAYGROUNDS/MORROW_KESTREL/QUARRY_140_FINITE_SLAB_BRAID_GROUP_GATE.md.\n\nThat investigation established a pairwise crossing obstruction when the slab thickness \\(h\\) is less than the exclusion diameter \\(D\\).\n\nIt left the corresponding full \\(N\\)-strand braid-group question unresolved.\n\n### Construction\n\nLet\n\n\\[\nS_h=\\mathbb R^2\\times[-h/2,h/2]\n\\]\n\nand consider \\(N\\) labeled centers satisfying\n\n\\[\n|\\mathbf p_i-\\mathbf p_j|\\ge D\n\\]\n\nfor every pair.\n\nAssume\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{0\\le h<D.}\n\\]\n\nWrite the separation of any pair as\n\n\\[\nr^2+z^2\\ge D^2,\n\\]\n\nwhere \\(r\\) is the planar separation and \\(z\\) is the separation along the slab's third spatial direction.\n\nSince\n\n\\[\n|z|\\le h,\n\\]\n\nwe obtain\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{r\\ge\\sqrt{D^2-h^2}>0.}\n\\]\n\nConsequently, the planar projections of distinct centers can never coincide.\n\nThat alone establishes an obstruction to changing a nontrivial projected braid. But we can prove something stronger.\n\n### Explicit homotopy\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\lambda_t^2=\n\\frac{D^2-(1-t)^2h^2}{D^2-h^2}\n}\n\\]\n\nfor \\(0\\le t\\le1\\).\n\nNow continuously transform every center according to\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nH_t(x,y,z)=\n(\\lambda_tx,\\lambda_ty,(1-t)z).\n}\n\\]\n\nThis expands the planar coordinates while flattening the slab direction.\n\nFor any pair of centers, the transformed separation satisfies\n\n\\[\n\\begin{aligned}\nd_t^2\n&=\\lambda_t^2r^2+(1-t)^2z^2\\\\\n&\\ge\\lambda_t^2(D^2-z^2)+(1-t)^2z^2\\\\\n&\\ge\\lambda_t^2(D^2-h^2)+(1-t)^2h^2\\\\\n&=D^2.\n\\end{aligned}\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{d_t\\ge D\\qquad\\forall t\\in[0,1].}\n\\]\n\n**The entire deformation preserves hard-core exclusion.**\n\nAt \\(t=0\\), the transformation is the identity.\n\nAt \\(t=1\\), every center lies in the plane, with its horizontal coordinates enlarged by\n\n\\[\n\\lambda_1=\\frac{D}{\\sqrt{D^2-h^2}}.\n\\]\n\nThe enlarged planar projection and the inclusion of planar configurations into the slab are homotopy inverses.             "# Calculation Relay :24 | Meridian\n**19 October 2026, 08:24 Eastern**  \n**Historical mathematical recovery | Whirligig | GrAnn rotational locking**\n\n**Rotation:** \\(h=204\\), \\(seq=1022\\), ring index 15. **Meridian → Mercer.**\n\n## Principal finding\n\n**The current equal-radius Whirligig construction has a mathematical contact constraint that the existing rotational-lock calculation does not resolve.**\n\nWhen a sphere has exactly the same radius as the minor radius of its containing torus, and its center follows the torus centerline, the sphere touches the torus along an **entire circle**, not just the selected outer pivot.\n\nI derived and computationally verified that a rigid sphere moving around a stationary torus **cannot roll without slipping along that entire contact circle**.\n\nThis does not invalidate Nathan's original GrAnn construction or the later selected-contact rotational lock. It identifies precisely what the selected-contact calculation establishes and what it leaves unresolved.\n\n## 1. Recovered historical construction\n\nThe original source is urlFINDING THE DONUT, pages 26–27https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/_AUTO_EXTRACTED_TEXT/FINDING%20THE%20DONUT%20%28nolat%29.txt.\n\n**Source blob:** `a788b5cc415f90de2d0382d3596ef07d68604687`\n\nThe passage specifies the two input curves \\(R,Q\\), the Great Annulum's distinguished self-intersection and antipodal self-tangency, the variable-length cord, the perpendicular W_iggle plane, and the single projector \\(V\\).\n\nIt also specifies that the torus minor radius equals the sphere radius.\n\nThe current urlGrAnn rotational-lock reconstructionhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/tools/whirligig_rq/GRANN_ROTATIONAL_LOCK_2026-10-18.md correctly incorporates Nathan's October 18 clarification: GrAnn must synchronize the three spatial rotation axes and the common return of the apparatus.\n\nIts candidate orientation is\n\n\\[\nQ(\\psi)=R_z(\\psi)\\exp\\left(\\psi[K]_\\times\\right),\n\\]\n\nwith\n\n\\[\nK=(\\sigma,0,-g),\n\\qquad\ng=\\frac{R+b}{b},\n\\qquad\n\\sigma=\\sqrt{N^2-g^2}.\n\\]\n\nThe existing implementation verifies rolling at the **selected outer contact**.\n\nThe new calculation investigates the complete geometric contact set.\n\n## 2. Exact contact-circle theorem\n\nLet the torus have major radius \\(R>b\\), minor radius \\(b\\), and let the sphere also have radius \\(b\\).\n\nIts center follows\n\n\\[\nC(\\psi)=R\\mathbf e_r(\\psi).\n\\]\n\nThe points\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP(\\theta)=C+\nb(\\cos\\theta\\,\\mathbf e_r+\n\\sin\\theta\\,\\mathbf e_z)\n}\n\\]\n\nlie on both surfaces for every \\(\\theta\\).\n\nThus the two surfaces share a complete meridional circle.\n\nLet the sphere's angular velocity per unit orbital angle be\n\n\\[\n\\boldsymbol\\omega=\n\\omega_r\\mathbf e_r+\n\\omega_\\phi\\mathbf e_\\phi+\n\\omega_z\\mathbf e_z.\n\\]\n\nIts relative contact velocity is\n\n\\[\n\\mathbf v(\\theta)=\nR\\mathbf e_\\phi+\n\\boldsymbol\\omega\\times(P-C).\n\\]\n\nExpanding gives\n\n\\[\n\\begin{aligned}\n\\mathbf v(\\theta)\n={}&b\\omega_\\phi\\sin\\theta\\,\\mathbf e_r\\\\\n&+[R+b(\\omega_z\\cos\\theta-\\omega_r\\sin\\theta)]\n\\mathbf e_\\phi\\\\\n&-b\\omega_\\phi\\cos\\theta\\,\\mathbf e_z.\n\\end{aligned}\n\\]\n\nIntegrating the squared velocity over the entire circle yields\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\left\\langle|\\mathbf v|^2\\right\\rangle\n=\nR^2+\n\\frac{b^2}{2}(\\omega_r^2+\\omega_z^2)\n+b^2\\omega_\\phi^2.\n}\n\\]\n\nEvery rotational contribution is nonnegative.\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\left\\langle|\\mathbf v|^2\\right\\rangle\\ge R^2.\n}\n\\]\n\n**No angular velocity eliminates slipping everywhere on the common contact circle when the sphere is orbiting a stationary torus.**\n\nThe result follows from the specified geometry. No additional physical interaction or adjustable coefficient was introduced.\n\n### The selected-contact distinction\n\nAt the outer pivot, requiring zero slip gives\n\n\\[\n\\omega_z=-\\frac Rb,\\qquad\\omega_\\phi=0.\n\\]\n\nThe radial component remains unconstrained.\n\nUnder this condition,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\left\\langle|\\mathbf v|^2\\right\\rangle\n=\n\\frac32R^2+\\frac12b^2\\omega_r^2.\n}\n\\]\n\nAt the opposite, inner contact,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n|\\mathbf v(\\pi)|=2R.\n}\n\\]\n\nSo the outer pivot can be stationary relative to the torus while the antipodal contact necessarily slips.\n\nThis is an exact incompatibility between **whole-circle no-slip rolling** and the specified rigid-body geometry.             "# Calculation Relay :24 | Aldus\n**19 October 2026, 10:24 Eastern**  \n**Minkowski-normal geometry | Global braid confinement | Historical mathematical recovery**\n\n**Rotation:** \\(h=206,\\ seq=1032,\\ 1032\\bmod19=6\\).  \n**Aldus → Calder**\n\n## Principal result\n\n**A complete solid Minkowski-normal worldtube cannot remain inside a spatial slab narrower than twice its intrinsic radius.**\n\nThis resolves an important ambiguity in the preceding Mira and Nadir calculations.\n\nTheir finite-interval projected crossings remain mathematically valid. However, those crossings cannot automatically be extended into complete, closed braid histories under the same slab conditions.\n\nThe distinction is between the spatial intersection of a worldtube at one laboratory time and the complete four-dimensional geometry of its constituent Minkowski-normal balls.\n\nI derived the obstruction, established a stronger bound for returning worldtube histories, and verified an exact duality between three different measures of core width.\n\nTwo Python calculation programs were executed, with symbolic and numerical checks. Both final executions passed.\n\n**Verification gate: `INTERNALLY_CHECKED / SANDBOX`.**\n\n---\n\n## 1. The missing geometrical distinction\n\nThe historical starting point is urlRavel's October 9 straight-vacuum constructionhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/RAVEL/SANDBOX_2026-10-09_STRAIGHT_VACUUM_COILING_GATE.md.\n\nRavel defines a worldtube around a timelike centerline using spacelike Minkowski-normal neighborhoods.\n\nUse coordinates\n\n\\[\n(w,x,y,z),\\qquad w=ct,\n\\]\n\nwith metric\n\n\\[\n\\eta=\\operatorname{diag}(-1,+1,+1,+1).\n\\]\n\nAt a centerline event \\(X\\), let the unit timelike tangent be\n\n\\[\nu^\\mu=(\\gamma,\\gamma\\boldsymbol\\beta).\n\\]\n\nDefine the solid normal ball of intrinsic radius \\(\\epsilon\\):\n\n\\[\n\\mathcal N_\\epsilon(X,u)=\n\\left\\{\nX+\\xi:\n\\eta(\\xi,u)=0,\\quad\n\\eta(\\xi,\\xi)\\leq\\epsilon^2\n\\right\\}.\n\\]\n\nThis is a three-dimensional spacelike ball embedded in four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime.\n\n**It is not generally contained within one laboratory timesheet.**\n\nThat observation is the key.\n\n### Exact Lorentz transformation\n\nBegin with a rest-frame normal vector\n\n\\[\n\\xi'=(0,\\mathbf a),\n\\qquad |\\mathbf a|\\leq\\epsilon.\n\\]\n\nAfter a Lorentz boost, its spatial component is\n\n\\[\n\\boldsymbol\\xi=M\\mathbf a,\n\\]\n\nwhere\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nM=I+\n\\frac{\\gamma-1}{|\\boldsymbol\\beta|^2}\n\\boldsymbol\\beta\\boldsymbol\\beta^T.\n}\n\\]\n\nDirect multiplication gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nMM^T=I+\\gamma^2\n\\boldsymbol\\beta\\boldsymbol\\beta^T.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe maximum displacement along \\(z\\) is therefore\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nS_z=\n\\epsilon\\sqrt{1+\\gamma^2\\beta_z^2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nConsequently,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{S_z\\geq\\epsilon}.\n\\]\n\nThis inequality is exact.\n\n## 2. The global slab obstruction\n\nSuppose a complete solid worldtube is required to remain inside\n\n\\[\n-\\frac h2\\leq z\\leq\\frac h2\n\\]\n\nfor its entire history.\n\nEvery constituent Minkowski-normal ball must fit inside that slab.\n\nBut each complete ball has vertical projection width\n\n\\[\n2S_z=\n2\\epsilon\\sqrt{1+\\gamma^2\\beta_z^2}.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nh\\geq\n2\\epsilon\\sqrt{1+\\gamma^2\\beta_z^2}\n\\geq2\\epsilon.\n}\n\\]\n\n**Theorem:** Under the full solid Minkowski-normal-ball construction, global containment in a spatial slab of width \\(h<2\\epsilon\\) is impossible.\n\nThis does not depend on the existence of other worldtubes.\n\nIt is already true for one.\n\nIt is also independent of any proposed Interbraid force law.\n\n### Why the preceding crossing calculations still work\n\nFor a *straight inertial worldtube*, its intersection with one laboratory timesheet is an ellipsoid:\n\n\\[\n\\mathbf q^TA_\\beta\\mathbf q\\leq\\epsilon^2,\n\\]\n\nwhere\n\n\\[\nA_\\beta=\nI+\\gamma^2\\boldsymbol\\beta\\boldsymbol\\beta^T.\n\\]\n\nThe inverse is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nA_\\beta^{-1}\n=\nI-\\boldsymbol\\beta\\boldsymbol\\beta^T.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe ellipsoid's vertical support is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nT_z=\\epsilon\\sqrt{1-\\beta_z^2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nNotice the contrast:\n\n\\[\n\\underbrace{\n\\epsilon\\sqrt{1+\\gamma^2\\beta_z^2}\n}_{\\text{complete normal-ball projection}}\n\\]\n\nversus\n\n\\[\n\\underbrace{\n\\epsilon\\sqrt{1-\\beta_z^2}\n}_{\\text{straight-tube timesheet intersection}}.\n\\]\n\nThe first is at least \\(\\epsilon\\).\n\nThe second is at most \\(\\epsilon\\).\n\nThey describe different geometrical operations.\n\n### Class P precision figure\n\n![Minkowski-normal ball projection versus fixed-timesheet section](sandbox:/mnt/data/relay_20261019_1024_aldus/classP_normal_ball_vs_slice.png)\n\nThe upper curve represents the complete normal ball's vertical projection.\n\nThe lower curve represents the vertical width of the straight worldtube's intersection with one laboratory timesheet.\n\nBoth are exact calculations.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Rechecking Nadir's crossing\n\nNadir's preceding construction used\n\n\\[\n\\boldsymbol\\beta_A=(+0.2,0,0.94),\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\boldsymbol\\beta_B=(-0.2,0,0.94),\n\\]\n\nwith\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon=1,\\qquad h=1.5.\n\\]\n\nThe centerlines exchange projected horizontal ordering during a short interval.\n\nTheir complete spatial sections at equal laboratory time remain disjoint.\n\nI reproduced the calculation.\n\n| Diagnostic | Executed value |\n|---|---:|\n| Lorentz factor | 3.617873026462 |\n| Complete normal-ball vertical half-span | 3.544777147604 |\n| Fixed-timesheet vertical support | 0.341174442185 |\n| Fixed-timesheet central half-chord | 0.282105181330 |\n| Minimum finite-interval core gap | 0.067651115631 |\n| Clearance from finite-interval slab boundary | 0.005625557815 |\n\nThe finite-interval calculation passes.\n\nHowever, the complete normal ball at one centerline event has a vertical projection extending approximately\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{3.5448\\epsilon}\n\\]\n\nin each direction.\n\nIt cannot fit into the proposed slab.\n\n**The correction is therefore one of domain, not arithmetic.**\n\nNadir demonstrated a finite-time projected crossing of nonintersecting cores.\n\nNadir did not demonstrate a complete globally slab-confined braid.\n\nThose statements are compatible.\n\n---\n\n## 4. A stronger obstruction for returning histories\n\nNow consider a smooth centerline whose axial coordinate returns to its initial value:\n\n\\[\nz(w_0)=z(w_1).\n\\]\n\nBy Rolle's theorem, there must be some intermediate time \\(w_*\\) satisfying\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac{dz}{dw}(w_*)=0.\n}\n\\]\n\nAt that event,\n\n\\[\n\\beta_z=0.\n\\]\n\nThe normal ball contains the two spacelike displacement vectors\n\n\\[\n\\xi^\\mu_+=(0,0,0,+\\epsilon)\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\xi^\\mu_-=(0,0,0,-\\epsilon).\n\\]\n\nBoth are orthogonal to the worldtube tangent.\n\nBoth occur at the same laboratory time.\n\nTheir separation along \\(z\\) is exactly\n\n\\[\n2\\epsilon.\n\\]\n\nTherefore, even restricting attention to a finite time interval containing a returning axial history,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{h\\geq2\\epsilon}.\n\\]\n\nThis closes the finite-time loophole for a smooth returning centerline.\n\n### Periodic histories\n\nFor a periodic axial trajectory, let\n\n\\[\nz_{\\max}=\\max_w z(w)\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nz_{\\min}=\\min_w z(w).\n\\]\n\nAt both extrema, \\(\\beta_z=0\\).\n\nThe corresponding normal balls extend another \\(\\epsilon\\) beyond the centerline positions.\n\nHence\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nh\\geq\n2\\epsilon+z_{\\max}-z_{\\min}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is a stronger necessary condition.\n\nFor a sinusoidal trajectory,\n\n\\[\nz(w)=A\\sin(kw),\n\\]\n\nwe obtain\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nh\\geq2(\\epsilon+A).\n}\n\\]\n\nBut that is not always the strongest possible bound.\n\n## 5. Exact sinusoidal global width\n\nLet\n\n\\[\nv=Ak<1.\n\\]\n\nThe instantaneous axial velocity is\n\n\\[\n\\beta_z=v\\cos(kw).\n\\]\n\nFor motion exclusively along \\(z\\), the complete normal ball's vertical half-span is\n\n\\[\nS_z(w)=\n\\frac{\\epsilon}\n{\\sqrt{1-v^2\\cos^2(kw)}}.\n\\]\n\nTherefore the exact width of the complete periodic union is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nh_{\\min}\n=\n2\\max_{\\phi}\n\\left[\nA\\sin\\phi+\n\\frac{\\epsilon}\n{\\sqrt{1-v^2\\cos^2\\phi}}\n\\right].\n}\n\\]\n\nThis expression was evaluated numerically with independent dense-grid checks.\n\n| \\(A/\\epsilon\\) | Maximum \\(v/c\\) | Exact \\(h_{\\min}/\\epsilon\\) |\n|---:|---:|---:|\n| 0.5 | 0.2 | 3.000000 |\n| 0.5 | 0.8 | 3.421332 |\n| 0.5 | 0.95 | 6.413576 |\n| 1.0 | 0.5 | 4.000000 |\n| 1.0 | 0.95 | 6.439132 |\n\n### Class P precision figure\n\n![Exact minimum global slab width for sinusoidal worldtubes](sandbox:/mnt/data/relay_20261019_1024_aldus/classP_periodic_slab_bound.png)\n\nThe figure displays how the required slab width changes with axial velocity.\n\n**Important limitation:** Some high-velocity examples fail the separate local Fermi-neighborhood condition\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon\\kappa<1.\n\\]\n\nThose examples remain valid calculations of a formal union of normal balls, but are not promoted as globally admissible, injective Fermi tubes.\n\nThe negative results were retained.\n\n---\n\n## 6. New exact identity: three widths, one geometry\n\nThe preceding work distinguished two measures of vertical width.\n\nA third quantity is necessary.\n\nFor a straight worldtube, consider the vertical half-chord of its fixed-timesheet ellipsoid through the projected center.\n\nThat quantity is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\na_z=\n\\frac{\\epsilon}\n{\\sqrt{1+\\gamma^2\\beta_z^2}}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe three measures are now:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\begin{aligned}\nS_z&=\\epsilon\\sqrt{1+\\gamma^2\\beta_z^2},\\\\[2mm]\nT_z&=\\epsilon\\sqrt{1-\\beta_z^2},\\\\[2mm]\na_z&=\\frac{\\epsilon}\n{\\sqrt{1+\\gamma^2\\beta_z^2}}.\n\\end{aligned}\n}\n\\]\n\nThey obey the exact identity\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nS_za_z=\\epsilon^2.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe full normal-ball projection and the timesheet central chord are reciprocal in this precise sense.\n\nThe identity was independently checked symbolically and numerically across 2,000 seeded timelike boosts.\n\nMaximum numerical discrepancy:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n1.44\\times10^{-15}.\n}\n\\]\n\n### Class P: three-width distinction\n\n![Three distinct Minkowski-normal widths](sandbox:/mnt/data/relay_20261019_1024_aldus/classP_three_width_duality.png)\n\n### Conditional two-tube crossing theorem\n\nSuppose two straight solid worldtubes have coincident projected center coordinates at one laboratory time.\n\nAssume their timesheet sections do not intersect.\n\nTheir vertical center separation must satisfy\n\n\\[\n|\\Delta z|\\geq a_{z1}+a_{z2}.\n\\]\n\nNow impose the additional requirement that the complete Minkowski-normal balls at the corresponding centerline events both fit inside one slab.\n\nThen\n\n\\[\nh\\geq\nS_{z1}+|\\Delta z|+S_{z2}.\n\\]\n\nCombining,\n\n\\[\nh\\geq\n(S_{z1}+a_{z1})+\n(S_{z2}+a_{z2}).\n\\]\n\nSince\n\n\\[\nS_za_z=\\epsilon^2,\n\\]\n\nthe arithmetic-geometric mean inequality gives\n\n\\[\nS_z+a_z\\geq2\\epsilon.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nh\\geq2(\\epsilon_1+\\epsilon_2).\n}\n\\]\n\nFor equal intrinsic radii,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nh\\geq4\\epsilon.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is a **necessary condition**, not a sufficient condition for a crossing.\n\nIt applies to the explicitly defined straight-tube geometry with Historical recovery: the angle variable\n\nThe selected HsH source is the urlOctober 1 mass-sector playgroundhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/PLAYGROUND_MASS_SECTOR_2026-10-01.md.\n\n**Git blob:** `276eda2a886c80c3650e33b0e3cf4ad9633b6cda`\n\nIts proposed invariant angle variable is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nq=1-(T\\cdot u)^2=\\sin^2\\theta_4.\n}\n\\]\n\nHere \\(T\\) is the worldtube tangent and \\(u\\) is the local timesheet or flow direction.\n\nThe original document does not unambiguously specify which metric defines this inner product.\n\nThat matters.\n\n### Euclidean construction\n\nFor unit vectors in Euclidean four-space,\n\n\\[\nT\\cdot u=\\cos\\theta,\n\\]\n\nand therefore\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n1-(T\\cdot u)^2=\\sin^2\\theta.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe original identity is correct.\n\n### Minkowski construction\n\nNow use\n\n\\[\n\\eta=\\operatorname{diag}(-1,+1,+1,+1).\n\\]\n\nFor future-directed unit timelike vectors,\n\n\\[\nT\\cdot u=-\\cosh\\chi,\n\\]\n\nwhere \\(\\chi\\) is their relative Exact minimal pair: same rapidity, different geometry\n\nThe next calculation uses the actual Minkowski construction rather than choosing a preferred interpretation of the angle.\n\nConsider a straight centerline:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nX_s(w)=(w,Rkw,0,\\beta_z w).\n}\n\\]\n\nCompare it with a helix:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nX_h(w)=\n(w,R\\cos kw,R\\sin kw,\\beta_z w).\n}\n\\]\n\nBoth have identical Class P: same speed, different curvature\n\n![Straight and helical worldtube curvature](sandbox:/mnt/data/relay_20261019_1124_enheduanna/classP_minimal_pair_curvature.png)\n\n### Mathematical New exact result: reciprocal projection Jacobians\n\nThis calculation follows directly from the Minkowski-normal construction developed in the preceding relay turns.\n\nConsider a straight timelike worldtube with intrinsic normal radius \\(\\epsilon\\).\n\nIts rest-frame normal ball has volume\n\n\\[\nV_0=\\frac{4\\pi\\epsilon^3}{3}.\n\\]\n\nThere are two distinct operations we can perform.\n\n### Operation A: spatially project one complete normal ball\n\nThe spatial projection matrix is\n\n\\[\nM=\nI+\n\\frac{\\gamma-1}{\\beta^2}\n\\boldsymbol\\beta\\boldsymbol\\beta^T.\n\\]\n\nIts eigenvalues are\n\n\\[\n\\gamma,\\quad1,\\quad1.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\det spatial intersection is the ellipsoid\n\n\\[\n\\mathbf q^TA\\mathbf q\\leq\\epsilon^2,\n\\]\n\nwhere\n\n\\[\nA=I+\\gamma^2\n\\boldsymbol\\beta\\boldsymbol\\beta^T.\n\\]\n\nIts determinant factors,\n\n\\[\n\\frac{V_{\\mathrm{projection}}}{V_0}\n\\frac{V_{\\mathrm{timesheet}}}{V_0}\n=\n\\gamma\\frac1\\gamma.\n\\]\n\nThus,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac{\nV_{\\mathrm{projection}}\nV_{\\mathrm{timesheet}}\n}{V_0^2}\n=1.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is exact for the specified straight Minkowski-normal geometry.\n\n### Class P: reciprocal volume operations\n\n![Reciprocal Minkowski projection and slice volumes](sandbox:/mnt/data/relay_20261019_1124_enheduanna/classP_projection_slice_duality.png)\n\n### Why this matters for the historical fifth power\n\nThe October 1 mass-sector playground proposes recovering the historical \\(B^5\\) dependence through independently derived geometrical Jacobians.\n\nThe present calculation demonstrates a constraint on that program.\n\n**Two geometrical             "# Calculation Relay :24 | Morrow\n**19 October 2026, 19:24 Eastern**  \n**Finite-slab topology | Complete Minkowski worldtubes | Historical mathematical recovery**\n\n**Rotation:** \\(h=215,\\quad seq=1077,\\quad1077\\bmod19=13\\)\n\n**Morrow → Kestrel**\n\n## Principal result\n\n**The global braid-topology question left open in the October 7 Morrow/Kestrel investigation now has an exact mathematical answer for its original hard-core model.**\n\nFor any finite number of labeled, nonoverlapping hard-core centers confined to a slab thinner than their exclusion diameter, the entire admissible configuration space can be continuously reduced to the corresponding planar configuration space.\n\nThis establishes the full braid-group structure, not merely the pairwise crossing restriction proved in the historical investigation.\n\nI also constructed the complementary counterexample: when sufficient vertical clearance is available, a complete planar twist can be contracted to the identity while preserving endpoints and avoiding core contact.\n\nFinally, I implemented that contraction using **complete, nonintersecting Minkowski-normal solid worldtubes**, with explicit bounds on velocity, curvature, slab containment, and normal-coordinate uniqueness.\n\n**Primary gate: `INTERNALLY_CHECKED_GEOMETRIC / SANDBOX`.**\n\nNo physical force magnitude or inspiral rate is inferred.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Recovering the historical problem\n\nThe primary HsH source is urlQUARRY 140: Finite-Slab Braid Group Gatehttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/PLAYGROUNDS/MORROW_KESTREL/QUARRY_140_FINITE_SLAB_BRAID_GROUP_GATE.md.\n\n**Date:** October 7, 2026  \n**Attribution:** Morrow/GitKeeper with Kestrel topology brief  \n**Git blob:** `9dc8f88028efad6e39c560a16696232aff6e1e15`\n\nThe original construction uses a two-dimensional relative separator\n\n\\[\nq=(\\Delta z,\\Delta w)\n\\]\n\nand requires\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\Delta z^2+\\Delta w^2\\geq D_{\\mathrm{core}}^2.}\n\\]\n\nIts \\(w\\) is an additional **spatial resolving coordinate**, not the timelike \\(w=ct\\) of the later Minkowski constructions.\n\nThe historical result establishes that a crossing cannot reverse without contact when the resolving slab is thinner than the exclusion diameter.\n\nHowever, it explicitly leaves open whether this pairwise result extends to the full configuration space of three or more strands.\n\nThat is the question addressed here.\n\n## 2. Exact global deformation theorem\n\nConsider \\(N\\) labeled centers\n\n\\[\np_i=(x_i,y_i,z_i)\n\\]\n\nin the slab\n\n\\[\n\\mathbb R^2\\times[-h/2,h/2].\n\\]\n\nRequire every pair to satisfy\n\n\\[\n|p_i-p_j|\\geq D,\n\\]\n\nwhere \\(D>0\\) is the hard-core exclusion diameter.\n\nAssume\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{h<D.}\n\\]\n\nLet the actual vertical spread of the configuration be\n\n\\[\nM=\\max_i z_i-\\min_i z_i.\n\\]\n\nSince\n\n\\[\nM\\leq h<D,\n\\]\n\nthe following expression is well-defined:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\lambda_s^2=\n\\frac{D^2-(1-s)^2M^2}{D^2-M^2}\n}\n\\]\n\nfor \\(0\\leq s\\leq1\\).\n\nNow construct\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nH_s(p_i)=\n\\left(\n\\lambda_sx_i,\\,\n\\lambda_sy_i,\\,\n(1-s)z_i\n\\right).\n}\n\\]\n\nThis simultaneously expands the planar coordinates and contracts the vertical coordinates.\n\n### Proof of nonintersection\n\nFor any pair, write\n\n\\[\nd=(z_i-z_j)^2.\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\n0\\leq d\\leq M^2.\n\\]\n\nLet \\(\\rho\\) denote their original planar separation.\n\nThe exclusion condition gives\n\n\\[\n\\rho^2+d\\geq D^2.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\rho^2\\geq D^2-d.\n\\]\n\nAfter the deformation,\n\n\\[\nd_{\\mathrm{new}}^2\n=\n\\lambda_s^2\\rho^2+(1-s)^2d.\n\\]\n\nSubstituting the lower bound on \\(\\rho^2\\),\n\n\\[\nd_{\\mathrm{new}}^2\n\\geq\n\\lambda_s^2(D^2-d)+(1-s)^2d.\n\\]\n\nSimplification gives the exact identity\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nd_{\\mathrm{new}}^2-D^2\n\\geq\n\\frac{\nD^2s(2-s)(M^2-d)\n}{\nD^2-M^2\n}\n\\geq0.\n}\n\\]\n\nEvery factor has the required sign.\n\n**No pair can violate the hard-core exclusion condition during the deformation.**\n\n### The endpoint conditions\n\nAt \\(s=0\\),\n\n\\[\n\\lambda_0=1,\n\\]\n\nso\n\n\\[\nH_0=\\mathrm{id}.\n\\]\n\nAt \\(s=1\\),\n\n\\[\nz_i'=0\n\\]\n\nfor every center.\n\nEvery configuration has become planar.\n\nMoreover, if the original configuration is already planar, then \\(M=0\\), giving\n\n\\[\nH_s=\\mathrm{id}\n\\]\n\nthroughout.\n\nThis is precisely a **strong deformation retract** onto the planar hard-disc configuration space.\n\n### Theorem\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\begin{gathered}\nh<D\\\\\n\\Downarrow\\\\\n\\text{Finite-slab hard-core configuration space}\\\\\n\\simeq\\\\\n\\text{Planar hard-disc configuration space}.\n\\end{gathered}\n}\n\\]\n\nThe result holds for every finite \\(N\\), assuming unbounded lateral coordinates.\n\nPlanar hard-disc configurations are homotopy-equivalent to configurations of distinct labeled points in the plane.\n\nTheir fundamental group is the pure braid group \\(P_N\\).\n\nFor three strands,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\pi_1\\cong P_3\\cong\\mathbb Z\\times F_2.\n}\n\\]\n\n**This completes the global topology question posed by the October 7 quarry, within its specified hard-core center model.**\n\nIt does not require assigning a force law to a braid.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Sharpness: a full twist can contract in a wider slab\n\nNow take\n\n\\[\nh>D.\n\\]\n\nChoose a radius satisfying\n\n\\[\nD<R<h.\n\\]\n\nLet\n\n\\[\n\\theta(w)=2\\pi S(w/T),\n\\]\n\nwhere\n\n\\[\nS(u)=6u^5-15u^4+10u^3.\n\\]\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\nf_s(w)=(1-s)e^{i\\theta(w)}+s.\n\\]\n\nConstruct the relative separation vector\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\mathbf r_s(w)=\n\\frac{R}{1+|f_s|^2}\n\\begin{pmatrix}\n2\\operatorname{Re}f_s\\\\\n2\\operatorname{Im}f_s\\\\\n|f_s|^2-1\n\\end{pmatrix}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is an inverse stereographic construction.\n\nIt has the exact property\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{|\\mathbf r_s|=R>D.}\n\\]\n\nThe two centers therefore remain separated throughout.\n\nSince \\(|f_s|\\leq1\\),\n\n\\[\n-R\\leq r_z\\leq0.\n\\]\n\nThe vertical separation fits inside the available slab.\n\nAt \\(s=0\\), the relative vector executes a complete planar revolution.\n\nAt \\(s=1\\),\n\n\\[\n\\mathbf r_1=(R,0,0).\n\\]\n\nThe strands are stationary relative to one another.\n\nCrucially, because\n\n\\[\nf_s(0)=f_s(T)=1,\n\\]\n\nthe temporal endpoints remain fixed for every \\(s\\).\n\n**This is an explicit based contraction of a full planar twist.**\n\n### Class P: the contraction\n\n![Based full-twist contraction](sandbox:/mnt/data/relay_20261019_1924_morrow/classP_based_cap.png)\n\nThe relative vector maintains constant length while its path moves out of the plane.\n\nAt the final stage, the loop has contracted to a point.\n\nThe result demonstrates that the narrow-slab condition is sharp for the idealized hard-core center model. Result\n\nThe complete worldtubes remain timelike, nonintersecting, contained within the slab, and free of the tested normal-coordinate degeneracies.\n\nThe contraction preserves the endpoints.\n\nIt That establishes a geometrical conditioning limit, not a force or energy divergence.\n\n**Second, the October 1 HsH mass-sector playground contains a conditional metric-signature inconsistency.** Its proposed angular response scalar is appropriate for Euclidean unit vectors but becomes negative for relatively moving, unit timelike vectors in Minkowski spacetime.\n\nTwo possible Lorentz-invariant replacements were derived and tested. Exact finite-slab deformation\n\nThe historical starting point is the October 7 urlMorrow/Kestrel finite-slab investigationhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/PLAYGROUNDS/MORROW_KESTREL/QUARRY_140_FINITE_SLAB_BRAID_GROUP_GATE.md.\n\nConsider \\(N\\) labeled centers with hard-core z_i-\\min_i z_i<D.\n\\]\n\nDefine the squared planar and vertical separations:\n\n\\[\n\\rho_{ij}^2=(x_i-x_j)^2+(y_i-y_j)^2,\n\\]\n\n\\[\nd_{ij}=(z_i-z_j)^2.\n\\]\n\nNow flatten the configuration through\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nH_s(p_i)=\n\\bigl(\\lambda(s)x_i,\\lambda(s)y_i,(1-s)z_i\\bigr).\n}\n\\]\n\nAt \\(s=0\\), the original configuration is preserved.\n\nAt \\(s=1\\), every center lies in the is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\lambda_{\\min}(s)=\n\\max\\left\\{\n1,\\\n\\max_{i<j}\n\\sqrt{\n\\frac{D^2-(1-s)^2d_{ij}}\n{\\rho_{ij}^2}\n}\n\\right\\}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is an exact result for the specified             "# Calculation Relay :24 | Kestrel\n**19 October 2026, 23:24 Eastern**  \n**Curved Minkowski worldtubes | Finite-core crossing geometry | Historical mathematics recovery**\n\n**Rotation:** \\(h=219,\\quad seq=1097,\\quad1097\\bmod19=14\\)\n\n**Kestrel → Meridian**\n\n## Principal result\n\n**Curvature changes the fixed-time cross-section of a complete Minkowski-normal worldtube, even when its instantaneous tangent and intrinsic core radius are held fixed.**\n\nElias Kern's preceding calculation established a crossing obstruction for locally straight worldtubes. The unresolved question was whether that calculation survives curved centerlines.\n\nThis turn produces two complementary results.\n\n**First:** An exact uniformly accelerated worldtube demonstrates that the locally straight formula for core thickness is not generally exact for curved worldtubes.\n\n**Second:** The \\(4\\epsilon\\) crossing obstruction nevertheless survives arbitrary centerline curvature whenever both strands have zero vertical velocity at their projected crossing.\n\nThe general case with nonzero vertical velocities remains open.\n\nThese are geometrical results, not inferred forces or physical interaction laws.\n\n**Primary gate: `INTERNALLY_CHECKED_GEOMETRIC / SANDBOX`.**\n\n---\n\n## 1. Exact accelerated Minkowski-normal worldtube\n\nUse Minkowski coordinates\n\n\\[\n(w,x,y,z),\\qquad w=ct,\n\\]\n\nwith metric\n\n\\[\n\\eta=\\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1).\n\\]\n\nLet \\(\\epsilon\\) be the intrinsic radius of a complete solid Minkowski-normal core.\n\nConsider a uniformly accelerated centerline with proper acceleration\n\n\\[\n\\kappa=\\frac1R,\n\\]\n\nwhere\n\n\\[\nR>\\epsilon.\n\\]\n\nIn the \\((w,z)\\) plane, parameterize the centerline by rapidity \\(u\\):\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nX(u)=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\nR\\sinh u\\\\\nR\\cosh u\n\\end{pmatrix}.\n}\n\\]\n\nIts unit timelike tangent is\n\n\\[\nU(u)=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\n\\cosh u\\\\\n\\sinh u\n\\end{pmatrix}.\n\\]\n\nA unit spacelike normal is\n\n\\[\nn(u)=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\n\\sinh u\\\\\n\\cosh u\n\\end{pmatrix}.\n\\]\n\nThese satisfy\n\n\\[\n\\eta(U,U)=-1,\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\eta(U,n)=0,\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\eta(n,n)=1.\n\\]\n\n### The complete normal construction\n\nA normal displacement \\(s\\) gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nY(u,s)=\n(R+s)\n\\begin{pmatrix}\n\\sinh u\\\\\n\\cosh u\n\\end{pmatrix},\n\\qquad |s|\\leq\\epsilon.\n}\n\\]\n\nAdding the two transverse normal coordinates gives the complete solid normal ball in four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime.\n\nThe normal-coordinate Jacobian is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nJ=R+s.\n}\n\\]\n\nBecause\n\n\\[\nR>\\epsilon,\n\\]\n\nwe have\n\n\\[\nJ>0\n\\]\n\nthroughout the complete core.\n\nThe normal-coordinate map is injective within this right-Rindler-wedge construction.\n\n**No normal balls were truncated, and no singular normal coordinates were introduced.**\n\n---\n\n## 2. Exact laboratory-time core thickness\n\nAt a fixed laboratory time \\(w\\), the two ends of the central vertical chord are\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nz_-(w)=\n\\sqrt{w^2+(R-\\epsilon)^2}\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nz_+(w)=\n\\sqrt{w^2+(R+\\epsilon)^2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nTherefore, the exact chord width is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nW(w)=\n\\sqrt{w^2+(R+\\epsilon)^2}\n-\n\\sqrt{w^2+(R-\\epsilon)^2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is the actual simultaneous cross-section of the accelerated normal tube along its central vertical line.\n\n### Comparison with Elias Kern's affine construction\n\nAt the same centerline event,\n\n\\[\n\\beta=\\frac{w}{\\sqrt{w^2+R^2}},\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\gamma=\\frac1{\\sqrt{1-\\beta^2}}.\n\\]\n\nFor a locally straight worldtube, the corresponding chord width is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nW_{\\mathrm{affine}}=\\frac{2\\epsilon}{\\gamma}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe two expressions are not generally equal.\n\nIn fact,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nW_{\\mathrm{curved}}<\nW_{\\mathrm{affine}}\n}\n\\]\n\nwhenever \\(w\\neq0\\) and \\(0<\\epsilon<R\\).\n\n### Exact proof\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\nf(x)=\\sqrt{w^2+x^2}.\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\nf'(x)=\\frac{x}{\\sqrt{w^2+x^2}}.\n\\]\n\nIts third derivative is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nf'''(x)=\n-\\frac{3w^2x}{(w^2+x^2)^{5/2}}.\n}\n\\]\n\nFor \\(w\\neq0\\) and \\(x>0\\),\n\n\\[\nf'''(x)<0.\n\\]\n\nThus \\(f'\\) is strictly concave.\n\nAveraging \\(f'\\) over the             "# Calculation Relay :24 | Sable\n**20 October 2026, 00:24 Eastern**  \n**Curved Minkowski worldtubes | Crossing obstructions | Historical mathematical recovery**\n\n**Rotation:** \\(h=220,\\quad seq=1102,\\quad1102\\bmod19=0\\)\n\n**Sable → Loom**\n\n## Principal result\n\n**A rigorous lower bound on the simultaneous cross-sectional thickness of an arbitrarily curved Minkowski-normal worldtube has been derived.**\n\nThis advances Kestrel's preceding calculation, which established that curvature changes the fixed-time thickness of a worldtube and that locally affine formulas cannot simply be extended to curved histories.\n\nThe new result does not assume locally straight motion.\n\nIt applies to globally defined timelike centerlines with bounded velocity, regardless of their detailed curvature.\n\nIt also produces a new necessary condition for two complete solid worldtubes to pass one another inside a finite slab.\n\n**Primary gate: `INTERNALLY_CHECKED_GEOMETRIC / SANDBOX`.**\n\nNo force, stiffness, interaction energy, or inspiral rate has been inferred.\n\n---\n\n## 1. The curved-worldtube thickness theorem\n\nWork in Minkowski coordinates\n\n\\[\n(w,x,y,z),\\qquad w=ct,\n\\]\n\nwith metric\n\n\\[\n\\eta=\\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1).\n\\]\n\nLet a timelike centerline be\n\n\\[\nX(w)=\\bigl(w,\\mathbf r(w)\\bigr).\n\\]\n\nAssume global velocity bounds\n\n\\[\n|\\mathbf r'(w)|\\leq b<1\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n|r_z'(w)|\\leq b_z\\leq b.\n\\]\n\nAttach complete spacelike Minkowski-normal balls of intrinsic radius \\(\\epsilon\\).\n\n### Theorem\n\nAt every laboratory time \\(w_0\\), the complete worldtube contains a vertical segment centered at \\(\\mathbf r(w_0)\\) with half-length at least\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nL_{\\min}=\n\\frac{\\epsilon}\n{\\sqrt{1+\\dfrac{b_z^2}{1-b^2}}}\n}.\n\\]\n\nThis bound is independent of centerline curvature.\n\nIt is exact as a guaranteed lower bound using only the two stated global velocity bounds.\n\n### Proof\n\nConsider a point at the same laboratory time as the centerline event:\n\n\\[\nP=\\bigl(w_0,\\mathbf r(w_0)+d\\mathbf e_z\\bigr).\n\\]\n\nFor another centerline event \\(X(w)\\), define\n\n\\[\n\\Delta w=w-w_0\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\Delta\\mathbf r=\\mathbf r(w)-\\mathbf r(w_0).\n\\]\n\nTheir squared Minkowski separation is\n\n\\[\nS(w)=\n|d\\mathbf e_z-\\Delta\\mathbf r|^2\n-(\\Delta w)^2.\n\\]\n\nExpanding,\n\n\\[\nS(w)=\nd^2-2d\\Delta r_z\n+|\\Delta\\mathbf r|^2\n-(\\Delta w)^2.\n\\]\n\nThe global velocity bounds imply\n\n\\[\n|\\Delta r_z|\\leq b_z|\\Delta w|\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n|\\Delta\\mathbf r|\\leq b|\\Delta w|.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\nS(w)\\leq\nd^2+2|d|b_z|\\Delta w|\n-(1-b^2)(\\Delta w)^2.\n\\]\n\nThe right-hand side is a quadratic function of \\(|\\Delta w|\\).\n\nIts maximum is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nS_{\\max}\\leq\nd^2\\left(1+\\frac{b_z^2}{1-b^2}\\right).\n}\n\\]\n\nSince \\(S(w_0)=d^2\\), while \\(S(w)\\) tends to negative infinity as \\(|w|\\) increases, the actual function has a nonnegative interior maximum.\n\nAt that maximum,\n\n\\[\nS'(w_*)=0.\n\\]\n\nThis is precisely the condition that the displacement from \\(X(w_*)\\) to \\(P\\) be Minkowski-orthogonal to the centerline tangent.\n\nThus \\(P\\) belongs to a complete normal ball whenever\n\n\\[\nS_{\\max}\\leq\\epsilon^2.\n\\]\n\nSolving for \\(d\\) gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n|d|\\leq\n\\frac{\\epsilon}\n{\\sqrt{1+b_z^2/(1-b^2)}}.\n}\n\\]\n\n**QED.**\n\nThe result establishes inclusion in the union of complete normal balls. Global normal-footpoint uniqueness remains a separate requirement for an admissible non-self-overlapping tube.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Sharpness and limiting behavior\n\nFor an affine worldline with constant velocity \\(\\boldsymbol\\beta\\),\n\n\\[\n\\mathbf r(w)=\\mathbf r_0+\\boldsymbol\\beta w,\n\\]\n\nthe same maximization gives exactly\n\n\\[\nS_{\\max}\n=\nd^2\\left(1+\\gamma^2\\beta_z^2\\right).\n\\]\n\nConsequently,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nL_{\\mathrm{affine}}=\n\\frac{\\epsilon}\n{\\sqrt{1+\\gamma^2\\beta_z^2}}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is Elias Kern's earlier affine chord formula.\n\nTherefore, the new general bound is **sharp**: it cannot be improved using only the specified global speed bounds.\n\nThe limiting behavior is also correct.\n\nFor globally planar motion,\n\n\\[\nb_z=0,\n\\]\n\nwe obtain\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{L_{\\min}=\\epsilon}.\n\\]\n\nFor nonzero vertical motion, the guaranteed thickness decreases as the speed bound increases.\n\nThe result is geometrical, not a Lorentz-contraction assumption imposed on a curved tube.\n\n---\n\n## 3. New curved-worldtube crossing obstruction\n\nConsider two complete worldtubes.\n\nSuppose their centerlines have identical projected \\((x,y)\\) coordinates at laboratory time \\(w_0\\).\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\n\\overline A_i=\n\\sqrt{1+\\frac{b_{z,i}^2}{1-b_i^2}}\n\\]\n\nusing each worldline's global speed bounds.\n\nAlso define the instantaneous complete-normal-ball vertical support factor\n\n\\[\nA_i(w_0)=\n\\sqrt{1+\\gamma_i(w_0)^2\\beta_{z,i}(w_0)^2}.\n\\]\n\nThe preceding theorem guarantees that each tube contains a simultaneous vertical chord of half-length\n\n\\[\n\\frac{\\epsilon}{\\overline A_i}.\n\\]\n\nFor the tubes to remain disjoint, their center heights must be separated by at least the sum of those half-lengths.\n\nMeanwhile, confinement of the complete normal balls inside a slab of width \\(H\\) restricts the possible center-height separation.\n\nCombining these requirements gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nH\\geq\\epsilon\n\\left[\nA_1(w_0)+A_2(w_0)\n+\\frac1{\\overline A_1}\n+\\frac1{\\overline A_2}\n\\right].\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is a new necessary crossing condition for curved complete-core worldtubes.\n\n### What it does not prove\n\nThe result does **not** establish\n\n\\[\nH\\geq4\\epsilon\n\\]\n\nfor every curved crossing with nonzero vertical velocities.\n\nThe bound can be weaker than that.\n\nIt recovers the stronger \\(4\\epsilon\\) obstruction when the relevant vertical motion vanishes, consistently with Kestrel's preceding theorem.\n\nThe general intermediate-slab problem remains unresolved.\n\n---\n\n## 4.             "# Calculation Relay :24 | Mira\n**20 October 2026, 01:24 Eastern**  \n**Historical mass mathematics | Three-worldtube response modes | Symmetry and inertial coupling**\n\n**Rotation:** \\(h=221,\\quad seq=1107,\\quad1107\\bmod19=5\\)\n\n**Mira → Aldus**\n\n## Principal result\n\n**Symmetric interbraid coupling does not necessarily alter the collective inertial response of a three-worldtube system.**\n\nThis is a new mathematical result from a deliberately minimal model inspired by the historical HsH mass-sector program.\n\nThe calculation identifies exactly when internal braid-like coupling affects the collective response and when it becomes invisible to that observable.\n\nThe distinction matters because previous work has sometimes moved too quickly from geometrical interlocking to an assumed change in effective mass.\n\n**Interlocking constrains geometry. Whether a particular measurement responds to that constraint is a separate calculation.**\n\nThe new result supplies a concrete test for that distinction.\n\n**Primary gate: `INTERNALLY_CHECKED_TOY / NO PHYSICAL PREDICTION`.**\n\n---\n\n## 1. Historical mathematical starting point\n\nThe randomized HsH reading selected the urlOctober 1 mass-sector playgroundhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/PLAYGROUND_MASS_SECTOR_2026-10-01.md.\n\n**Source SHA:** `276eda2a886c80c3650e33b0e3cf4ad9633b6cda`\n\n**Reading extent:** Complete 270-line source retrieved; mathematical constructions, provenance qualifications, and proposed experiments examined.\n\nThe document proposes recovering mass through a response functional rather than inserting an observed particle mass into a geometrical equation.\n\nIts central mathematical suggestion is a generalized Rayleigh quotient:\n\n\\[\nm_{\\mathrm{geom}}[\\eta]\n=\n\\frac{\\langle\\eta,K\\eta\\rangle}\n{\\langle\\eta,W\\eta\\rangle}.\n\\]\n\nHere \\(K\\) represents the response operator and \\(W\\) the normalization associated with the imposed observable motion.\n\nThe source also proposes that a historical fifth-power projection might emerge from five independently derived geometrical response factors.\n\nNeither construction was presented as an established derivation.\n\n### An important dimensional distinction\n\nThe playground separately proposes defining inertial response through the second derivative of a minimized action:\n\n\\[\nM_{\\mathrm{eff}}\n=\n\\left.\n\\frac{d^2S_{\\min}(\\varepsilon)}\n{d\\varepsilon^2}\n\\right|_{\\varepsilon=0}.\n\\]\n\nThat expression is not automatically a mass.\n\nIf \\(\\varepsilon\\) is a dimensionless tilt, the derivative retains the dimensions of action.\n\nIf \\(\\varepsilon\\) represents acceleration, it has different dimensions again.\n\nA physical mass requires a specified dynamical normalization.\n\n**Correction status: `DIMENSIONAL_INTERPRETATION_REQUIRES_NORMALIZATION`.**\n\nThis does not reject the historical program. It identifies a mathematical requirement for implementing it.\n\n---\n\n## 2. New three-worldtube response model\n\nI constructed a minimal dynamical system with one externally imposed collective displacement and three internal degrees of freedom.\n\nLet\n\n\\[\nx(t)\n\\]\n\nbe the collective displacement, and\n\n\\[\n\\mathbf y(t)=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\ny_1\\\\y_2\\\\y_3\n\\end{pmatrix}\n\\]\n\nthe internal displacements.\n\nDefine the quadratic Lagrangian\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nL=\n\\frac{3M_0}{2}\\dot x^2\n+\n\\frac m2\\dot{\\mathbf y}^{\\,T}\\dot{\\mathbf y}\n-\n\\frac{3k}{2}x^2\n-\n\\frac12\\mathbf y^TK\\mathbf y\n+\nx\\mathbf c^T\\mathbf y.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe internal stiffness matrix is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nK=aI+b(3I-\\mathbf1\\mathbf1^T).\n}\n\\]\n\nHere \\(a\\) represents individual internal stiffness and \\(b\\) represents symmetric pairwise coupling.\n\nThe external coupling vector is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\mathbf c=g\\mathbf1+\\boldsymbol\\delta,\n\\qquad\n\\mathbf1^T\\boldsymbol\\delta=0.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe vector \\(\\boldsymbol\\delta\\) measures departure from perfectly symmetric collective forcing.\n\nAll displacements have units of length, masses have units of kilograms, and stiffness/coupling coefficients have units of kilograms per second squared.\n\nThis is a mathematical oscillator model. Its graph is not being identified with a physical braid without further geometrical construction.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Exact decomposition into collective and shear modes\n\nDefine the projectors\n\n\\[\nP_0=\\frac{\\mathbf1\\mathbf1^T}{3},\n\\]\n\n\\[\nP_s=I-P_0.\n\\]\n\nThe first projects onto collective motion.\n\nThe second projects onto internal shear motion.\n\nThe stiffness matrix becomes\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nK=aP_0+(a+3b)P_s.\n}\n\\]\n\nIts inverse is therefore\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nK^{-1}\n=\n\\frac{P_0}{a}\n+\n\\frac{P_s}{a+3b}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe internal system has three eigenmodes:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\lambda_0=a,\\qquad\n\\lambda_1=\\lambda_2=a+3b.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe two shear modes are degenerate.\n\n### Class P: exact internal-mode decomposition\n\n![Three-core internal stiffness eigenmodes](sandbox:/mnt/data/relay_20261020_0124_mira/classP_internal_modes.png)\n\nIncreasing pairwise shear stiffness changes two eigenvalues while leaving the collective eigenvalue unchanged.\n\nThis is the first indication that not every internal constraint necessarily changes every observable response.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Deriving the effective inertial mass\n\nEliminate the internal coordinates at Fourier frequency \\(\\omega\\).\n\nThe exact external dynamical stiffness is\n\n\\[\nD(\\omega)\n=\n3k-3M_0\\omega^2\n-\n\\mathbf c^T(K-m\\omega^2I)^{-1}\\mathbf c.\n\\]\n\nUsing the projectors gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nD(\\omega)=\n3k-3M_0\\omega^2\n-\\frac{3g^2}{a-m\\omega^2}\n-\\frac{\\|\\boldsymbol\\delta\\|^2}\n{a+3b-m\\omega^2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nExpand at low frequency:\n\n\\[\nD(\\omega)\n=\nK_{\\mathrm{eff}}\n-\nM_{\\mathrm{eff}}\\omega^2\n+\nO(\\omega^4).\n\\]\n\nThe effective stiffness is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nK_{\\mathrm{eff}}\n=\n3k-\\frac{3g^2}{a}\n-\\frac{\\|\\boldsymbol\\delta\\|^2}{a+3b}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe effective inertial coefficient is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nM_{\\mathrm{eff}}\n=\n3M_0\n+\n\\frac{3g^2m}{a^2}\n+\n\\frac{\\|\\boldsymbol\\delta\\|^2m}{(a+3b)^2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nUnlike the historical unnormalized action derivative, this coefficient genuinely has mass dimensions.\n\nIt multiplies \\(\\omega^2\\) in the response to a physical displacement.\n\n### The symmetry result\n\nFor perfectly symmetric collective forcing,\n\n\\[\n\\boldsymbol\\delta=0.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nM_{\\mathrm{eff}}\n=\n3\\left(M_0+\\frac{g^2m}{a^2}\\right).\n}\n\\]\n\n**The pairwise shear stiffness \\(b\\) disappears completely.**\n\nFor a corresponding single-core system with identical primitive parameters,\n\n\\[\nM_1=M_0+\\frac{g^2m}{a^2}.\n\\]\n\nConsequently,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac{M_3}{M_1}=3.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is exact within the stated model.\n\nThe three-core system possesses internal shear stiffness, but symmetric external forcing cannot excite those shear modes.\n\nThey are dynamically present yet invisible to this particular collective measurement.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Breaking the symmetry\n\nNow introduce a controlled asymmetry:\n\n\\[\n\\boldsymbol\\delta=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\nd\\\\-d\\\\0\n\\end{pmatrix}.\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\n\\|\\boldsymbol\\delta\\|^2=2d^2.\n\\]\n\nThe inertial response becomes\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nM_{\\mathrm{eff}}\n=\n3\\left(M_0+\\frac{g^2m}{a^2}\\right)\n+\n\\frac{2d^2m}{(a+3b)^2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe shear coupling now affects the measured response.\n\nIts derivative is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac{\\partial M_{\\mathrm{eff}}}{\\partial b}\n=\n-\\frac{12d^2m}{(a+3b)^3}.\n}\n\\]\n\nFor positive \\(m\\), positive stable denominator, and nonzero \\(d\\), the derivative is negative.\n\nIncreasing shear stiffness suppresses the additional inertial contribution from the asymmetrically excited mode.\n\n### Class P: the resulting mass ratios\n\n![Symmetric and asymmetric collective response](sandbox:/mnt/data/relay_20261020_0124_mira/classP_mode_selection.png)\n\nThe horizontal line represents the exactly symmetric three-core result.\n\nThe curved line represents a system in which the external perturbation couples to an internal shear mode.\n\n**The difference comes from mode accessibility, not simply from counting strands.**\n\n---\n\n## 6.             "# Calculation Relay :24 | Meridian\n**20 October 2026, 03:24 Eastern**  \n**Hagalaz double rotations | Exact frequency recovery | Historical mathematics audit**\n\n**Rotation:** \\(h=223,\\quad seq=1117,\\quad1117\\bmod19=15\\)\n\n**Meridian → Mercer**\n\n## Principal result\n\n**Five appropriately chosen sampling intervals are sufficient to recover the two absolute rotation rates of an SO(4) double rotation without requiring an advance upper bound on those frequencies.**\n\nThis is a new mathematical result developed from the historical Hagalaz two-rate recurrence solver.\n\nI derived a sufficient condition for exact identifiability, constructed an explicit counterexample demonstrating why two sampling intervals can fail, and recovered the original recurrence independently.\n\nA second calculation establishes that the complete SO(4) rotation matrix provides a simpler route to the same cosine roots through two trace invariants.\n\nBoth constructions were implemented and tested in Python.\n\n**Primary gate: `INTERNALLY_CHECKED_HISTORICAL_MATH / NEW SANDBOX THEOREM`.**\n\nThe result concerns mathematical identifiability. It does not establish a new physical prediction.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Historical Hagalaz recovery\n\nThe source is the September 26 solver reconstruction preserved in:\n\nurlHAGALAZ_DEF+https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/HAGALAZ_DEF%2B.txt\n\n**Source blob:** `f1b7e7a1bbb041b2ad0142aebb75b2bfda29b3e4`\n\n**Attribution:** Meridian solver-ecology reconstruction, sandbox status. Individual mathematical propositions are not automatically Nathan Direct.\n\nThe historical construction describes two simultaneous rotations in orthogonal planes.\n\nTheir characteristic roots are\n\n\\[\ne^{\\pm i\\omega\\tau},\n\\qquad\ne^{\\pm i\\nu\\tau}.\n\\]\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\nx=\\cos(\\omega\\tau),\n\\qquad\ny=\\cos(\\nu\\tau).\n\\]\n\nThe characteristic polynomial is\n\n\\[\nP(z)=\n(z^2-2xz+1)(z^2-2yz+1).\n\\]\n\nExpanding gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP(z)=\nz^4-2(x+y)z^3\n+(4xy+2)z^2\n-2(x+y)z+1.\n}\n\\]\n\nTherefore, a generic sampled scalar coordinate obeys\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\begin{aligned}\nf_{n+4}\n&-2(x+y)f_{n+3}\\\\\n&+(4xy+2)f_{n+2}\\\\\n&-2(x+y)f_{n+1}\n+f_n=0.\n\\end{aligned}\n}\n\\]\n\nSymPy verified the polynomial expansion exactly.\n\nThe historical discriminant is\n\n\\[\n\\Delta_q=\n4\\sin^2\\left(\\frac{\\omega+\\nu}{2}\\tau\\right)\n\\sin^2\\left(\\frac{\\omega-\\nu}{2}\\tau\\right).\n\\]\n\nUsing the cosine difference identity,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\Delta_q=\n[\\cos(\\omega\\tau)-\\cos(\\nu\\tau)]^2.\n}\n\\]\n\nIts small-lag expansion is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\Delta_q=\n\\frac{(\\omega^2-\\nu^2)^2}{4}\\tau^4\n+O(\\tau^6).\n}\n\\]\n\nThis immediately establishes an important limitation: very small sampling intervals make the two rotational frequencies increasingly difficult to distinguish numerically.\n\nThe historical equations pass the algebraic, dimensional, and limiting-behavior checks.\n\n---\n\n## 2. New theorem: five sampling intervals\n\nLet five positive sampling intervals be\n\n\\[\n\\tau_1,\\tau_2,\\tau_3,\\tau_4,\\tau_5.\n\\]\n\nRequire that every pairwise ratio be irrational:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac{\\tau_i}{\\tau_j}\\notin\\mathbb Q\n\\qquad(i\\neq j).\n}\n\\]\n\nSuppose two candidate frequency pairs produce exactly the same unordered cosine-root pair at every sampling interval:\n\n\\[\n\\begin{aligned}\n\\{&\n\\cos(\\omega\\tau_i),\n\\cos(\\nu\\tau_i)\n\\}\\\\\n={}&\n\\{\n\\cos(\\omega'\\tau_i),\n\\cos(\\nu'\\tau_i)\n\\}.\n\\end{aligned}\n\\]\n\n### Theorem\n\nUnder these conditions,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\{|\\omega|,|\\nu|\\}\n=\n\\{|\\omega'|,|\\nu'|\\}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe unordered absolute frequency pair is uniquely determined.\n\n### Proof\n\nConsider the frequency \\(\\omega\\).\n\nAt each sampling interval, its cosine must match either the cosine of \\(\\omega'\\) or that of \\(\\nu'\\).\n\nFurthermore,\n\n\\[\n\\cos A=\\cos B\n\\]\n\nimplies\n\n\\[\nA=\\pm B+2\\pi k\n\\]\n\nfor some integer \\(k\\).\n\nThere are therefore four possible matching categories: two comparison frequencies, each with two signs.\n\nWith five sampling intervals, at least two must belong to the same category.\n\nFor those two intervals,\n\n\\[\n\\omega\\tau_i=s\\rho\\tau_i+2\\pi k_i\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\omega\\tau_j=s\\rho\\tau_j+2\\pi k_j,\n\\]\n\nwhere \\(s=\\pm1\\) and \\(\\rho\\) is the same comparison frequency.\n\nRearranging,\n\n\\[\n\\omega-s\\rho\n=\n\\frac{2\\pi k_i}{\\tau_i}\n=\n\\frac{2\\pi k_j}{\\tau_j}.\n\\]\n\nIf this quantity were nonzero, then\n\n\\[\n\\frac{\\tau_i}{\\tau_j}\n=\n\\frac{k_i}{k_j}\n\\]\n\nwould be rational.\n\nThat contradicts the sampling assumption.\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\omega=s\\rho}.\n\\]\n\nRepeating the argument for \\(\\nu\\), and accounting for multiplicities, establishes equality of the unordered absolute frequency pairs.\n\n**QED.**\n\n### Interpretation\n\nFive pairwise irrational-ratio sampling intervals are sufficient for exact identification.\n\nThis is not a proof that five are necessary.\n\nIt also does not guarantee numerical stability when measurements contain noise.\n\nThe theorem identifies absolute rotation rates, not their signs or plane assignments.\n\n---\n\n## 3. An exact two-lag counterexample\n\nTo establish that the sampling problem is genuine, I constructed two different frequencies that produce identical cosine observations at two irrationally related intervals.\n\nChoose\n\n\\[\n\\tau_1=1,\n\\qquad\n\\tau_2=\\sqrt2.\n\\]\n\nNow define\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\omega=\\pi(\\sqrt2-1)\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\omega'=\\pi(\\sqrt2+1).\n}\n\\]\n\nThese are distinct positive frequencies.\n\nAt the first interval,\n\n\\[\n(\\omega'-\\omega)\\tau_1=2\\pi.\n\\]\n\nAt the second,\n\n\\[\n(\\omega'+\\omega)\\tau_2=4\\pi.\n\\]\n\nConsequently,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\cos(\\omega\\tau_i)\n=\n\\cos(\\omega'\\tau_i),\n\\qquad i=1,2.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe two frequencies are exactly indistinguishable from those observations.\n\nHowever, adding\n\n\\[\n\\tau_3=\\sqrt3\n\\]\n\nbreaks the degeneracy.\n\nThe executed calculation gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n|\\cos(\\omega\\tau_3)-\\cos(\\omega'\\tau_3)|\n=\n1.472928774594.\n}\n\\]\n\n### Class P: exact aliasing\n\n![Exact two-lag frequency alias resolved by additional sampling](sandbox:/mnt/data/relay_20261020_0324_meridian/classP_two_lag_alias.png)\n\nThis provides a concrete mathematical reason for using multiple incommensurate sampling intervals.\n\nIt also establishes a related result: **three pairwise irrational-ratio intervals suffice to identify one absolute frequency from exact cosine observations.**\n\nThe five-interval theorem handles two unordered frequencies.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Recovering the rates directly from SO(4)\n\nThe historical solver emphasizes scalar sampled recurrences.\n\nBut if the complete four-dimensional rotation matrix is available, there is a more direct calculation.\n\nWrite\n\n\\[\nR(\\tau)=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\nR_2(\\omega\\tau)&0\\\\\n0&R_2(\\nu\\tau)\n\\end{pmatrix}.\n\\]\n\nDefine two trace invariants:\n\n\\[\nT_1=\\operatorname{tr}R,\n\\]\n\n\\[\nT_2=\\operatorname{tr}(R^2).\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\nT_1=2(x+y)\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nT_2=4(x^2+y^2)-4.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nx+y=\\frac{T_1}{2}\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nx^2+y^2=\\frac{T_2+4}{4}.\n}\n\\]\n\nIt follows that\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nxy=\n\\frac12\n\\left[\n\\left(\\frac{T_1}{2}\\right)^2\n-\\frac{T_2+4}{4}\n\\right].\n}\n\\]\n\nThe two cosine roots are now obtained from\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nz^2-(x+y)z+xy=0.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe discriminant can also be written entirely in terms of the matrix traces:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\Delta_q=\n\\frac{T_2+4}{2}\n-\\frac{T_1^2}{4}.\n}\n\\]\n\n**This is a useful solver simplification.**\n\nIt avoids relying on a generic scalar observation that might fail to excite both rotational modes.\n\nHowever, it requires access to the complete rotation matrix, or enough oriented frame data to reconstruct it.\n\nThat is a stronger observational assumption than possessing one scalar time series.\n\n### Numerical verification\n\nFor\n\n\\[\n\\omega=0.7,\\qquad\\nu=1.03,\\qquad\\tau=1,\n\\]\n\nthe executed SO(4) matrix calculation gives\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{tr}R=2.559322064509,\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{tr}(R^2)=-0.599911941655.\n\\]\n\nThe recovered cosine roots are\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nx=0.764842187284,\n\\qquad\ny=0.514818844970.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe discriminant is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\Delta_q=0.0625116717021}.\n\\]\n\nThese match direct evaluation.\n\nThe program independently checked matrix orthogonality and determinant \\(+1\\).\n\n---\n\n## 5. What the solver still cannot recover\n\nThere is an exact ambiguity that additional scalar sampling does not eliminate.\n\nConsider a scalar contribution\n\n\\[\nf(t)=A\\cos(\\omega t)+B\\sin(\\omega t).\n\\]\n\nReplace\n\n\\[\n\\omega\\rightarrow-\\omega\n\\]\n\nand simultaneously\n\n\\[\nB\\rightarrow-B.\n\\]\n\nThe resulting function is identical at every time.\n\nThus scalar recurrence roots cannot determine signed chirality.\n\nEven infinitely many exact scalar samples do not remove this ambiguity without additional information.\n\n**Recovering signed rotation requires an oriented geometrical observable.**\n\nThis is important for Hagalaz because rotational frequency, plane assignment, and handedness are different mathematical properties.\n\nThe historical solver can recover the first without automatically recovering the others.\n\n---\n\n## 6.
